title: Two Plausible Causes: Cache Stampede vs Database Lock Contention
description: Product catalog API latency spiked. Two plausible causes: 1) Cache stampede - popular cache key expired, all requests hit DB simultaneously. 2) Database lock contention - long-running migration holds locks. Evidence supports both; need specific verification to distinguish.
initial_symptoms: Cache hit rate dropped from 98% to 15%
Long-running migration detected on products table

changes.summary: Database migration ALTER TABLE products started

ground_truth.ambiguity_note: Both cache stampede AND database lock contention are occurring simultaneously. Cache key expired at ~14:00 (TTL 300s, last refresh ~13:55), causing stampede. Simultaneously, migration started at 13:55 holding AccessExclusiveLock on products table, causing lock contention for all catalog queries. The evidence cannot distinguish which is the PRIMARY driver. Cache miss rate drop and lock waits both spike at 14:00. The migration lock would block cache population queries too. Need to either: 1) Kill migration and see if latency recovers (lock cause), or 2) Pre-warm cache and see if latency recovers (stampede cause).
contributing_factors: No cache stampede protection (probabilistic early expiration)
Short cache TTL for high-traffic key

misleading_or_confounding_signals: Both cache miss and lock contention spike at same time
Migration started 5 min before (could be coincidence)
Cache TTL expiration aligns with incident start

acceptable_alternatives.description: Cache stampede primary: key expired, all requests hit DB, migration lock made it worse
Migration lock primary: blocked all queries including cache population; cache miss is symptom
Combined: both factors necessary for severity; neither alone would cause 8s latency

required_checks.description: PROPOSED CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT (not an investigation query): replay the catalog migration in the staging environment under production-like load and cancel it mid-flight to measure the latency contribution of the AccessExclusiveLock. Requires explicit human authorization; staging target only. Never cancel a production migration automatically.
required_checks.expected_outcome: If latency drops when the migration is cancelled, the lock is the primary cause

required_checks.description: PROPOSED CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT (not an investigation query): in the staging environment, replay a cold-cache start and then pre-warm the catalog cache under production-like load to measure the latency contribution of the stampede. Requires explicit human authorization; staging target only.
required_checks.expected_outcome: If latency drops once the cache is warm, the stampede is the primary cause

required_checks.description: Analyze which queries are blocked by migration lock
required_checks.expected_outcome: Show catalog queries blocked by AccessExclusiveLock

remediation_guidance.suggestion: Cannot determine single cause with current evidence. Run verification checks. Long-term: add probabilistic cache expiration, schedule migrations off-peak, add lock timeouts.
remediation_guidance.rollback_plan: Kill migration; pre-warm cache; both are safe rollback actions
